issue.description:
Field evidence gathered 2026-10-23 on codinghome: a sweep of all 92 bead-rs workspaces under /home/coding, git object accounting in the largest repos, and every bead invocation in agent transcripts under ~/.claude/projects (32,149 calls) and ~/.codex/sessions (80,311 calls). Counts are regex-based and approximate.

Problem: the durable checkpoint often never reaches git. 42 of 92 workspaces have a git-committed `.beads/checkpoint/current.json` at least 7 days older than the live one (19 more are 1-6 days behind). devimprint has never committed one. claude-print's last checkpoint commit is 2026-09-17, despite commits landing daily since.

Cause: ADR-018 auto-stages the published fileset and relies on the next commit to carry it, but this environment's standing rule is precise-path commits (`git commit <paths>`), and a pathspec commit ignores everything else staged. `bead sync commit` exists for exactly this (a bead-only pathspec), yet agents invoked it 54 times in 112k bead calls. Nothing tells the operator how stale the git copy is: `sync status` reports staged/committed groups and a yes/no verdict, never the age or the generation gap that makes the problem actionable.

Scope:
- `sync status` adds the committed generation (the one named by HEAD's `.beads/checkpoint/current.json`, or `never`), the number of published generations since it, and the age of the oldest uncommitted generation. Text form: one `Committed:` line. JSON form: a `committed` object.
- `doctor` emits a `WARN ` line naming `bead sync commit` when that age exceeds `checkpoint.commit_lag_warn_seconds` in .beads/config.json (default 86400), or when nothing has ever been committed while generations exist.
- Revise the sync-status sections of research/specs/needle-cli-contract-v1.md and checkpoint-set-v1.md to match.
- Must agree with beadrs-71121ad2 (the false `Ready to commit: yes`), which edits the same verdict and lands first.

Acceptance:
- Git fixtures: never committed; committed at generation N with live at N+3; fully committed. Each reports the exact gap and age in text and JSON.
- A pathspec commit of an unrelated file leaves the reported gap unchanged; `bead sync commit` clears it to zero.
- doctor WARNs past the threshold and is silent below it; the threshold is configurable; no `.beads` content is ever printed.
- No git binary, or a workspace outside a repository, keeps exit 0 with `unavailable` (existing contract).
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test pass.
issue.notes: Scope addition (2026-10-23, filer), reproduced live in bead-rs: after 'bead sync commit' (commit 4e911f94, generation gen-52110464371936b22f7178de9e8da080, live = covered = sequence 28168), sync status still reports 'Git: staged' and 'Ready to commit: NO'. The two remaining staged entries are deletions of superseded objects (objects/60e04286...jsonl and objects/d97a093b...jsonl). Both are unreferenced by HEAD's current.json and previous.json, yet still tracked at HEAD. sync commit's help says its pathspec includes 'the removal of every tombstoned object Git tracks', but these removals were not carried, and sync status counts them as pending. So 'ready' is unreachable through the sanctioned command, and the lag this bead reports could never return to zero. Acceptance addition: after 'bead sync commit' on a fixture that has superseded tracked objects, sync status reports Ready to commit: yes and a committed gap of 0, and sync commit and sync status agree on exactly which removals belong to the fileset.
issue.title: Report how far the git-committed checkpoint trails the live checkpoint in sync status and doctor

SECTION 2: Immutability of comment bodies - VERDICT: MATCH

SECTION 3: Author attribution - VERDICT: MATCH
Clauses: ladder --actor > BEAD_ACTOR > system with trim-to-decide-presence; verbatim storage; 255-byte cap; create/reply actor becomes author + event actor; resolve/unresolve actor in event only; actor scanned on every command.
Observed (ladder driven live, authors read back via show --comments all):

- create/reply: audit event actor == resolved author for every rung (events 45-51). Reply event detail = {"comment_id":"comment-5e753a56","reply_to_id":"comment-1944d7fe"} - both IDs, no body.
- resolve/unresolve: author 'env-actor-1' unchanged through resolve+unresolve; events carry actor 'reviewer-7' only. Repeat resolve: exit 0, semantic_change:false, emitted no event.
- Actor scanned on every command: guard_pairs(conn, selector, actor, pairs) passes actor as a dedicated scanned field on create/reply AND resolution (src/service/secret_boundary.rs:110); CLI canonical_request has Command::Comment arms (src/cli_secret_scan.rs:299,443).

- All four subcommands carry about + long_about + EXAMPLES blocks in house style; `bead comment --help` lists all four.

(Pre-existing, out-of-scope observation: the list already had two inversions before R010 - 'redact'>'recurrence', 'restore'>'resource' - neither involves comment; flagged here so a reconciliation child does not mistake them for R010 regressions.)
- Field guide: checkpoint_issue.comments operations = comment.create/comment.reply/comment.resolve/comment.unresolve (src/service/schema.rs:1552); snapshot digests refreshed at 6878c2ae and validated by the suite (see verified block).
- Consumer contract: research/specs/needle-cli-contract-v1.md contains zero 'comment' references and was last touched by R025 commit 7c4d60b1 - untouched as specified.

- Clause: "The `comment` noun and each subcommand carry `about` and `long_about` with EXAMPLES blocks in the established house style (see the `restore` long-about)".
- Observed: the noun's long_about (src/cli.rs:145-163, shown verbatim by `bead comment --help`) carries all four enumerated content elements - what it writes, what it refuses to write, the body transports, the actor ladder - plus a four-line command synopsis, but has NO literal 'EXAMPLES:' block. issue.description:
ADR-001 is Accepted and explicitly defers the work to 'post-0.1 item R025', but no open bead tracks it — every sibling ADR item (R026, R028, R030, R035, R036) has one. Add `verifies` as a third dependency kind beside `blocks`/`relates_to`: schema plus migration, checkpoint round-trip, `bead dep` CLI surface, audit events, and unchanged cycle rejection. Add a structural diagnosis that reports a `blocks` edge whose blocker `verifies` its blocked bead (an inverted verification gate) via `bead doctor`/list output — advisory only, never rejected at insert, and never inferred from issue titles. Include concurrency tests for edge insertion, round-trip fixtures, and help/spec documentation. Motivating field evidence: 21 and 24 inverted edges found in two live workspaces, silently wedging the ready frontier.
